extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and institutions applying for IES education research and training grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting applications to the Institute of Education Sciences (IES) research and research-training grant competitions, including unsolicited submissions. Covers procedural steps, eligibility limits, submission systems, and policies applicants must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify a current funding opportunity that matches research interests and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Find an opportunity that matches your research interests and the deadlines for that opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search for Requests for Applications (RFAs) and use the ALN codes (for example ALN 84.305 or ALN 84.324) to find the correct competition and deadlines. Future RFAs will be listed as available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the IES Application Submission Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: The IES Application Submission Guide provides information on how to prepare and submit applications through Grants.gov to IES research and research training grant programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this guide to learn about IES-specific guidance and recommendations to help ensure your application is complete and submitted on time. See the Request for Applications for your competition for important information about substantive requirements and submission deadlines. Download the FY2025 Application Submission Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Download and complete the correct application package
rubrics_metrics.description: Download the application package for the appropriate ALN (e.g., 84.305 or 84.324).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search for the Request for Applications and the application package associated with the ALN for your program. Submit materials according to the package instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register or update your organization on Grants.gov and SAM.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: Register or update your organization on Grants.gov and SAM.gov before applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Grants.gov and SAM.gov registration steps early. Read the Department's Fact Sheet on the transition from DUNS Number to Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). Ensure organizational registration is current prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit application to Grants.gov before the application deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your application to Grants.gov before the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload important documents and submit early enough to resolve any technical issues. The IES Application Submission Guide and the specific RFA state deadline details. 'Submit documents before your deadline' is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit required documents (including optional LOI) as instructed
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload important documents and submit your Letter of Intent (LOI) — optional but strongly encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While LOIs may be optional, IES 'strongly encourages' submitting one; if you miss an LOI deadline contact the program officer for guidance. Follow RFA instructions for all required/uploaded documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow substantive requirements in the Request for Applications (RFA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request for Applications for each competition contains important substantive requirements and submission deadlines that applicants must follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the RFA for competition-specific eligibility, required components, evaluation criteria, page limits, and submission instructions; the Application Submission Guide supplements RFA instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific peer review administered by the Office of Science
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Science is responsible for the scientific peer review process for grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should learn about the peer review process (see Peer Review Process and lists of peer reviewers) and watch the 'After Submitting an IES Application' video to understand what happens post-submission. Prepare applications with typical scientific review expectations in mind (rigor, significance, clarity) even though detailed review criteria are in the RFA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsolicited application eligibility — not eligible under FY2025 competitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Unsolicited applications will be considered only for projects that are not eligible under IES's FY2025 grant competitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must demonstrate that their project was not eligible under one of the FY2025 grant competitions. If the project would be eligible for an FY2025 competition, it should be submitted to that competition instead of as unsolicited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsolicited applications must include student education outcomes when required
rubrics_metrics.description: A project that lacks student education outcomes and would be eligible under an FY2025 competition if student education outcomes had been included is not eligible as an unsolicited project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that unsolicited proposals include the outcome measures that would be expected in the comparable competition; absence of required student outcomes can render a submission ineligible as unsolicited.

rubrics_metrics.name: No funding for projects consisting solely of program delivery or services to students
rubrics_metrics.description: IES does not provide funds for projects that consist solely of program delivery or the provision of services to students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities supported by IES must be research, evaluation, or statistics projects relevant to education; proposals that are purely operational implementation or service delivery are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities supported must be relevant to U.S. schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities supported by IES must be relevant to U.S. schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsolicited and competitive projects alike should demonstrate relevance to U.S. education contexts and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsolicited will not accept proposals that would have been eligible under prior IES competitions/topics not run in FY2025
rubrics_metrics.description: IES will not consider applications under this unsolicited announcement that in prior years would have been eligible under IES competitions or topics that are not being run in FY2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes, but is not limited to, programs irregularly competed in prior years (examples: NCER's Postdoctoral Education Research Training program ALN 84.305B; NCSER's Postdoctoral Research and Methods Training programs ALN 84.324B). Check current FY2025 competition list before submitting unsolicited proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions may submit multiple applications only if substantively different
rubrics_metrics.description: An institution may submit multiple applications to a single IES grant program, or to a single topic within a grant program, only if the applications are substantively different from one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid submitting duplicate or marginally different proposals to the same program/topic; ensure each application has distinct aims or approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and federal rights to products developed with grant funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Products derived from IES-funded grants may be copyrighted and used by the grantee for proprietary purposes, but the U.S. Department of Education reserves a royalty-free, non-exclusive, and irrevocable right to reproduce, publish, or otherwise use such products for Federal purposes and to authorize others to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware of 2 C.F.R. § 200.315(b) and the Department's retained rights when planning dissemination, commercialization, or proprietary use of project outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of non-U.S. institutions and training grant geographic limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: You may apply to most IES grant programs if your institution is not located in the United States; however, IES awards training grants only to institutions within the territorial United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact program officers for clarification about eligibility if located outside the territorial United States; training grant opportunities (research training programs) are restricted geographically.
